description: Gossip propagation flavor text. After a moral choice resolves and propagatesOnDay arrives, the world reacts through camp chatter, NPC greeting changes, and whispered reputation. The player never sees their score — only these reactions.

camp_chatter.description: Ambient lines overheard in camp after gossip propagates. Sorted by moral band at time of propagation.
very_positive: Did you hear? They gave their last medicine to that stranger's kid. The whole course.
The one from the eastern shelter — people say they buried every body they found on the ridge. Every one.
Someone told me they sat with old Mara all night. Didn't ask for anything. Just sat.
I heard they turned down a clean trade route to carry a wounded stranger back to camp. On their back.
The Peacekeepers are talking about them. Not the bad kind of talking.
Word is they gave seeds to the last farmer on the plateau. The whole stock. Their own stock.
They say even the raiders won't touch that one. Too much... weight, I guess. Too much weight behind the name.
A child in the east quarter drew a picture of them. Calls them 'the kind one.' Hangs it on the wall.
The Knowledge Keepers want to meet them. Not to ask — to give. That's new.
I don't trust saints. But this one keeps showing up, and keeps giving, and hasn't asked for a single thing back.
They gave the clinic its last clean bandage roll and waited for the next shipment.
The outer-gate watch says they carried a frightened stranger in before checking their papers.
They returned the trade scale with the extra measure still on it.
Someone saw them leave the warm bunk for a sick traveler and never mention it.
They kept the promise even after the promised thing became scarce.
The ration pot went short, and they still put the youngest plates first.
They let the wounded rival cross the yard under their protection.
The repair crew got the part they needed because this one surrendered a useful spare.
They told the truth about the missing cans before anyone had to ask.
A lot of people talk brave; that one paid the cost and kept the door open.
positive: They helped the Peacekeeper on the north road. Shared supplies, I heard. Not nothing.
People say they listened to old Gregor's war story. The whole thing. Even the ugly parts.
Word around camp — they comforted the widow by the east fire. Sat with her through the bad hours.
The merchant at the crossroads gives them a nod now. Fair trader, apparently.
I heard they buried a body near the water tower. Properly. Not just kicked dirt over it.
Someone said they gave food to that raider with the broken gun. The raider told them about the next raid.
The doctor at the clinic speaks well of them. Something about patience. About listening.
They stopped for the thirsty one on the desert road. Gave water. Got directions to a spring.
Not a saint. But decent. That's worth noting, these days.
The trade scale came back honest after they used it. The next crew noticed.
They brought a spare lamp to the night watch instead of waiting for the fire to fail.
The clinic got first pick of the clean cloth. Nobody had to argue for it.
They stopped to carry a tired traveler through the gate and still made the meeting on time.
They left room in the bunk row for people who had not arrived yet.
They answered the hard questions without turning the whole thing into a performance.
Someone says they sent word before changing the ration list. That counts as courtesy now.
They had leverage and did not use all of it.
They returned a borrowed tool before the repair shift asked for it.
The route note was shared with the next crew. No price attached.
They remembered who had been waiting when the meeting ran long.
slightly_positive: They helped someone on the road. I forget who. But they helped.
People say they're not bad. Which is... something.
The Peacekeepers don't frown when that name comes up. Low bar, but there it is.
I heard they gave a little food to a stranger. Not much. But they gave.
Someone said they listened to a story or two. Didn't mock anyone for telling one.
Could have kept the whole crate. Didn't.
I heard they waited their turn at the clinic.
They asked what was needed before offering what they had.
The gate stayed open for one more person, apparently because they asked.
They corrected the count when nobody else noticed.
Not generous, exactly. Just less hard than expected.
Someone got a second chance after they listened.
They let a stranger finish speaking before walking away.
The deal was fair enough that nobody checked the pockets twice.
They shared the route note, then acted like it was nothing.
They carried one end of the stretcher. The other end did most of the work.
The request was small, and they did not make it smaller.
They gave back the tool with the blade still sharp.
They could have made a scene. They chose the quieter answer.
'Maybe they are learning,' someone said. Nobody argued.
neutral: Who? Oh, them. I don't know. They come and go. Keep to themselves.
Never helped me. Never hurt me. That's the whole file on them.
The name doesn't ring any bells. Which is probably fine.
Neither the raiders nor the Peacekeepers mention them. That's a kind of safety.
Average. In the old world that was an insult. Now it's a blessing.
Ask three people what they think and get four answers.
They'll help if the numbers work. That's not nothing.
The door opens for some requests and stays shut for others.
They trade clean, but they don't promise clean.
Nobody knows whether the pause means caution or indifference.
They keep a ledger. So does everyone who plans to last.
One crew calls them fair; another calls them difficult.
The answer changes when the weather does.
They listen until the cost becomes clear.
Somebody got shelter. Somebody else got a refusal.
They brought supplies in and questions out.
The same decision looks wise from one bunk and cold from another.
They do not explain every choice, which leaves room for everyone else's version.
If there is a pattern, it has not shown itself to me.
Wait for the next request. That is usually where the truth is.
slightly_evil: Watch your gear around that one. I'm not saying they took anything. I'm saying watch it.
They walked past someone on the road. I saw it. Just walked past.
People say they refused a child. Could be rumor. Could be fact. The child remembers.
The merchant at the crossroads doesn't give them credit anymore. Something happened.
I don't like the look they give people who ask for help. The look says 'no' before the mouth does.
Count your filters before you hand them over.
They keep the letter of a promise and lose the part that mattered.
Someone asked for help and got a price list instead.
They remember who cannot afford to refuse.
The door opened after the argument, not before.
They do not raise their voice; they just make the alternative smaller.
Keep a second route in mind when they offer the first.
The ration list changed after one name disappeared from it.
They call it efficiency when someone else goes without.
The apology came after the supplies were already gone.
Nobody says betrayal yet. They are waiting to see if it becomes a habit.
A promise from them needs a witness now.
The outer watch learned not to ask twice.
They offered a choice with only one affordable answer.
'Don't make them angry' is becoming part of the instructions.
evil: Stay away from that one. I mean it. People who cross their path end up lighter.
They took from the injured man on the east road. Took his pack while he watched.
Word is they robbed the Knowledge Keeper. Ripped the notes right out of their hands.
The Peacekeepers have a description circulating. Matches that one pretty well.
A raider told me even their people talk about this one — and not with admiration. With caution.
Someone died on the south road. Didn't have to. This one walked past, pockets heavier than before.
The farmer's seed locker is empty. You know who did it. I know who did it. The fence knows.
Don't trade with them. The last person who did found their kit missing the next morning.
People lower their voices when that patrol comes through.
The clinic started counting its bandages before answering their knock.
They call a threat a negotiation and wait for gratitude.
The trader's new escort is not for the road. It is for meetings here.
A surrender is only an invitation to lose something, according to them.
The outer bunks empty when their people ask for space.
They keep the useful part of every bargain and forget the promise.
Someone stopped carrying a family name in public after dealing with them.
No one volunteers a shortage around that table.
They took the safe route off the map and charged for directions.
The apology was posted beside the new lock.
Their offers sound generous until you count who cannot refuse.
very_evil: Lock your shelter. That one is in the area.
The Peacekeepers posted a bounty. You know whose face is on it.
I watched them take from a dying woman. Her last bundle. While she tried to curse them.
The raiders respect them. Think about what that means. Think hard.
A child won't go near the east path anymore. Says 'the bad one' lives there.
They say you can trade with them — but only if you have something they can't just take.
The Knowledge Keepers tell their children about this one. As a warning.
Someone put a mark on the wall outside their shelter. A red mark. Everyone knows what it means.
The old man by the fire stopped telling stories. Says there's no point. Not with this one around.
Even the dogs cross the road when they see them coming. Animals know.
No one leaves a child alone near the outer door when their shadow is on the road.
The traders bring an escort and a second set of scales.
People erase names from the request board before this one can read them.
The lower room fills early whenever their delegation is expected.
They do not ask what a person can spare. They ask what can be taken.
A friendly wave from that direction means check the exits.
Witnesses stopped signing the ledger. They know where the pages go.
The camp keeps a quiet route for anyone who needs to disappear.
Somebody moved the clinic stores before the meeting began.
They call it peace when everyone else has run out of choices.

npc_greeting_shifts.description: How NPCs change their opening line when greeting the player after gossip propagates.
very_positive: Oh — you're the one they talk about. The kind one. What can I do for you?
I heard what you did for the family on the ridge. Thank you. Truly.
You don't have to buy anything. Sit. Eat. You've earned that much.
My daughter drew a picture of you. She's never met you. That's how far your name travels.
The Peacekeepers told us about you. We saved you a share. Here.
You made it. Come in before the cold takes the choice out of your hands.
We've got a place by the stove. Take it; nobody is keeping score.
Tell me what the clinic needs. We'll sort our share first.
You're welcome at this table. If you brought trouble, we can talk about that too.
I heard you kept the gate open. What can I set aside for you?
Good morning. You look tired; use the good cup.
We can start with the difficult part. I won't make you earn the conversation.
There is room inside. Bring whoever is waiting with you.
You have my attention. Take the time you need.
If you need a witness, I will stand there.
No need to bargain over the first bowl. Eat.
You kept your word before. Let's see what you need today.
Come closer; the fire is shared.
We saved the clean bandages for people who come back through the gate. Take some.
You can ask plainly here. Plain answers are still available.
positive: Ah, you. I've heard good things. What do you need?
The merchant said you trade fair. That's enough for me. What can I offer?
You helped someone I know. So I'll help you. Fair's fair.
I trust you more than most. Which isn't saying much, but it's saying something.
Morning. Need the fair price or the honest directions?
Good to see you. We can work something out.
Someone vouched for you at the gate. Start with what you need.
Come in; the door is open while you are here.
I kept your last message. What changed?
You can look over the stock before we name a price.
If this is about the clinic, I can point you to the right queue.
We have a little time. Use it well.
I can spare a hand, a can, or an answer. Which one?
You don't have to explain the whole road. Tell me where it hurts.
The watch knows your name. You won't be delayed.
Trade first, questions after, unless you want it the other way.
You showed up when it mattered. What matters now?
Take the dry seat. We can talk over the noise.
If someone sent you, say who. If you came yourself, that's fine too.
You are still welcome to ask.
slightly_positive: You seem alright. What are you after?
Haven't heard anything bad about you. That's practically a recommendation.
You can sit if you want. Fire's open.
Come in if you like. I can spare a minute.
You kept that last answer simple. Let's try again.
I remember you. That is not a complaint.
You can stand by the door or take the chair. Your choice.
Need something? Say it before I decide what you mean.
We can talk. Just don't promise more than you can carry.
You returned the tool, so I am listening.
I have not forgotten the fair count.
Start with the part that costs you.
You can ask for help without making a speech.
I was expecting worse. Good morning.
If you are here to trade, set it down where I can see it.
There is room at the edge of the fire.
You did one decent thing. Let's not spend it twice.
I can give you an answer, maybe not the one you want.
We have met before. Try not to make this awkward.
Say what you need; I will decide what I can spare.
neutral: What do you want?
Trading or passing through?
I don't know you. State your business.
Sit if you want. Leave if you want. Makes no difference to me.
You're here. What do you need?
We can talk. Keep it brief.
If you are trading, show the goods.
I have a few minutes. Use them carefully.
What brings you to this door?
You know the arrangement. State your request.
Sit or stand; either way, say what this is about.
I can listen before I decide.
No promises from either side. That works for me.
You want something. Start there.
The ledger is open. The answer may not be.
If this is a complaint, make it specific.
We have dealt before. Let us see if that helps.
You can ask. I can say no.
The room is public; the conversation is not.
Tell me what changed since last time.
slightly_evil: Keep your distance. We can talk from here.
I know your face. I'll trade, but I'm watching my pack.
What do you want? Make it quick.
The children go inside when you come around. You notice that?
We can talk from here. Do not cross the line.
Set the pack down before you sit.
I remember the last promise. Bring a witness this time.
Make your request and keep your hands visible.
There is no reason to raise your voice. There is also no reason to trust it.
You get the outer table. The inner door stays shut.
If you want credit, bring someone who can vouch for you.
Do not make me count the supplies twice.
You can trade, but nothing leaves this room unmarked.
I have heard enough versions. Give me the one you can prove.
Keep to the lit side of the yard.
Ask for what you need, not what you think we owe.
You are allowed to speak. That is not the same as being agreed with.
The children are inside. Choose your words.
We will finish this before the watch changes.
If you came for forgiveness, find another door.
evil: You. I know what you did. Say your piece and go.
My hand's on my knife. Don't take it personally. Actually, do.
Last person who looked at me like that lost a tooth. State your business.
I'd spit, but you're not worth the moisture.
State your business. The inner door stays closed.
Leave the pack where I can see it.
You get one answer. Make it useful.
Do not call this a favor.
We remember the last deal. You do not get the soft version.
The watch will hear this conversation.
If you are asking for supplies, bring the count and the reason.
No room at this table. Use the public bench.
You can speak; nobody promised to help.
Do not reach for the ledger.
The gate is open for trade, not trust.
If you came to bargain, start with what you owe.
Keep your voice down. I do not want this mistaken for welcome.
The clinic will see you after the others. You know why.
Leave before someone thinks I invited you.
We are not discussing what happened. We are discussing what you will do now.
very_evil: Get away from my fire. Now.
I know your face. Everyone does. The bounty poster made sure of that.
You come any closer and I scream. The whole camp comes running.
I have nothing you can take. Leave.
The mark on my door is for you. You know what it means. Walk on.
Stop at the line. I will find someone else to hear you.
The fire is not yours. Keep walking.
You can leave your message with the watch.
Do not say my name like we are friends.
The door stays shut. So does the conversation.
Take one more step and the whole yard hears it.
We moved the stores before you arrived.
If you need help, ask someone who still trusts you.
No trade here. Not after the last one.
You may wait outside until daylight.
Do not bring a child to this door.
Whatever you want, the answer is no.
I will not be alone for this conversation.
The room is full. It was full before you came.
Leave the marker where you found it and go.

whisper_lines.description: Lines murmured between NPCs when the player passes by. The player catches fragments.
very_positive: ...gave everything they had, I heard...
...the Peacekeepers want to meet them, not arrest them...
...buried every body on the ridge. Every single one...
...sat with the old woman all night. Didn't sleep...
...even the raiders won't...
...a saint, or the closest thing we have left...
...gave the last clean blanket to someone from outside...
...they waited for the answer, even when it hurt...
...the spare part went to the clinic first...
...kept the promise after the price changed...
...the gate watch says they never asked who deserved it...
...they listened before they chose...
...the little one got the warm bunk...
...returned the extra measure...
...not loud about it. That's why people believe it...
...the rival crossed safely because they said so...
...they could have taken the credit...
...someone had to give up a route. They did...
...you can still trust a promise if that one makes it...
...the good news travels farther when no one is paid to carry it...
positive: ...fair trader, they say...
...helped the doctor's patient. Didn't ask for pay...
...listened to old Gregor. The whole damn story...
...gave water to the one on the road...
...fair count, fair price...
...they brought the clinic what it needed...
...someone got a second chance...
...they came back with the missing names...
...the door was open when the family arrived...
...they did not press the wounded traveler...
...you can ask them straight...
...the trade crew stopped checking the seal twice...
...a promise kept is still news...
...they left enough for the next shift...
...the answer was kind without making a show of it...
...they remembered the small things...
...the watch lets them pass without a question...
...they share the route if you ask...
...not perfect. Reliable is enough...
...they help before anyone has to beg...
slightly_positive: ...could have kept it...
...they gave the extra back...
...maybe I was wrong...
...don't make a song of it. They helped...
...they listened all the way through...
...the fair count held...
...they let the stranger finish...
...one more place at the table, that's all...
...the deal did not turn ugly...
...they left the tool where it belonged...
...not generous. Just decent for once...
...the door stayed open a little longer...
...they gave an answer before taking anything...
...I expected a sharper edge...
...the second chance was real...
...they shared the map and asked for nothing...
...the promise cost them. They paid it...
...someone spoke up for them...
...it was a small kindness...
...wait and see if it happens again...
neutral: ...who? Oh, nobody special...
...comes and goes...
...I don't know them. Do you?...
...depends who is asking...
...fair in one room, stubborn in the next...
...they keep their reasons to themselves...
...someone got help. Someone else got a refusal...
...the door is open until it isn't...
...watch what happens when the cost changes...
...no one can agree what they want...
...the same story has three endings...
...they count the cans before they count the people...
...not cruel. Not kind. Careful...
...ask again tomorrow...
...they will trade, but not explain...
...one decision does not make a pattern...
...the camp has not chosen what to call them...
...the answer was practical. That is all...
...if you know what they need, you know what they will do...
...keep listening. The next choice matters more...
slightly_evil: ...didn't help, I heard...
...walked past someone. Just walked past...
...the merchant watches their hands now...
...count your own supplies...
...the promise bends when they need it...
...someone asked twice and still left empty-handed...
...don't hand over the whole bundle...
...the door opened after the price went up...
...they call it a choice...
...the watch learned to stand closer...
...keep a witness nearby...
...you can hear the apology coming after the damage...
...they know who cannot say no...
...one favor, three strings...
...the missing name was not an accident...
...no one wants to be first to complain...
...their kindness has a receipt...
...ask what happens if you refuse...
...they do not need to threaten you twice...
...we are not calling it betrayal yet...
evil: ...took from the dying one...
...the Keeper screamed for an hour after...
...lock your things tonight...
...the Peacekeepers are circulating a description...
...the clinic is counting before they answer...
...don't show them the full pack...
...they call it a bargain after taking the choice away...
...the watch turns people around at their door...
...someone stopped using their real name...
...the room empties when they arrive...
...keep the family out of the meeting...
...they remember debts and forget the help...
...no one volunteers a shortage...
...the trader brought an escort...
...the apology came with a new lock...
...they asked what could be spared, then decided...
...the surrender did not end the asking...
...people are weighing exits now...
...the safe route vanished from the map...
...you can hear the fear in the polite answers...
very_evil: ...that's them. Don't look. Don't look...
...the bounty says alive, but I've heard 'dead' works too...
...even the raiders are careful around...
...took a child's toy from a grave. A grave...
...I won't sleep until they're gone from this camp...
...the lower room first...
...do not leave the ledger out...
...the escort is not for the road...
...people stop speaking when that door opens...
...move the children before the meeting...
...they will call it an offer...
...nobody signs their name near that mark...
...wait until the yard is empty...
...hide the spare key...
...the trader brought two guards...
...let them think the shelves are bare...
...somebody moved the clinic stores...
...do not tell them who is missing...
...if they smile, check the exits...
...keep the children away from the door...

gossip_decay.description: Gossip intensity fades over time. After 30 days without a new resolution, gossip downgrades one intensity level. After 60 days, it reaches baseline (neutral greetings). A single dramatic act resets the clock.
